messages.author: 4201c816d32af2ef
messages.subject: setMergeGroups error?
parts:
Hi.

Just processing a small number of exon arrays for the first time and
am having trouble getting the residuals. Was planning to process them
both as 'exons' and as 'transcripts'.

Below are my commands, then the error, then my 'sessionInfo()'.

Thanks,
Mark

------------- # begin my commands
verbose <- Arguments$getVerbose(-8); timestampOn(verbose)
name <- "heart_brain"
chipType <- "HuEx-1_0-st-v2"

cs <- AffymetrixCelSet$fromName(name, chipType=chipType)

coreChipType <- paste(chipType, "core", sep=",")
cdf <- AffymetrixCdfFile$fromChipType(coreChipType)

setCdf(cs, cdf)

qn <- QuantileNormalization(cs, typesToUpdate="pm")
csN <- process(qn, verbose=verbose) #time required

plm.merge <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=TRUE)
plm.nomerge <- ExonRmaPlm(csN, mergeGroups=FALSE)

fit(plm.merge, verbose=verbose) #time required
fit(plm.nomerge, verbose=verbose) #time required

rs <- calculateResiduals(plm.merge, verbose=verbose)
------------- # end my commands


> rs <- calculateResiduals(plm.merge, verbose=verbose)
Error in setMergeGroups(paf, this$mergeGroups) :
no applicable method for "setMergeGroups"
> rs <- calculateResiduals(plm.nomerge, verbose=verbose)

parts:
Hi Henrik,
I just installed the new version (0.4.9) and I'm still getting the error
for 'setMergeGroups' on the probe affinity file...(I had already used an
old version to calculate the residuals and weights). Looking at the
function 'getProbeAffinityFile.ExonRmaPlm', there is no place where the
class is set to 'ExonProbeAffinityFile'; and there is an argument
'.class=ExonProbeAffinityFile' which is never passed to any function. Maybe
paf <- NextMethod("ProbeAffinityFile", this, ...)
in the code should be
paf <- NextMethod("getProbeAffinityFile", this, .class=.class, ...)
That seemed to correct the problem for me and be more in line with
'getChipEffectSet'.
Sorry for another problem!
Elizabeth

parts:
Hi,

thanks for the report. I apparently need to get some redundancy tests
for the exon too, because now my test script only catch non-exon bugs.

Instead of uploaded a new version immediately, I've made a patch
available. Just do the following in your working directory:

> library(aroma.affymetrix)
> downloadPackagePatch("aroma.affymetrix")
trying URL 'http://www.braju.com/R//patches/aroma.affymetrix/20070424/ExonRmaPlm
.R'
Content type 'text/plain' length 7909 bytes
opened URL
downloaded 7909 bytes
> quit()

This will create a subdirectory 'patches/' with code patches for the
version of the package you're running. Then *RESTART* R, and you
should see:

> library(aroma.affymetrix)
Loading required package: R.oo
...
aroma.affymetrix v0.4.9 (2007-04-22) successfully loaded. See ?aroma.affymetrix
for help.
Patching patches/aroma.affymetrix/20070424/ExonRmaPlm.R
>

So, every time you load the package the patches will be loaded.

Hope this works

Henrik
